evidence_text: There is no reliable scientific evidence that turmeric (haldi), turmeric milk (haldi doodh), or curcumin alone can cure or treat cancer in humans.
While curcumin has shown antioxidant properties in laboratory studies, clinical trials have not demonstrated that turmeric cures malignant tumors.
Cigarette smoking is the leading cause of lung cancer, linked to approximately 80% to 90% of lung cancer deaths.
Tobacco smoke contains more than 7,000 chemicals, at least 69 of which are known to cause cancer in humans and animals.
Multiple rigorous scientific studies involving millions of children over decades have found no causal link between vaccines and autism.
Extensive scientific research by the Institute of Medicine has demonstrated that vaccines and vaccine ingredients do not cause autism.
Vaccines are rigorously evaluated for safety and provide high efficacy in preventing life-threatening infectious diseases.
Antibiotics treat bacterial infections only; they do not kill viruses or cure viral infections such as the common cold, flu, or viral bronchitis.
Taking antibiotics for viral illnesses will not cure the infection, will not prevent others from getting sick, and can cause unnecessary side effects.
Antibiotic overuse for viral infections accelerates antibiotic resistance, rendering crucial medicines ineffective against serious bacterial threats.
There is currently no permanent herbal cure for diabetes; diabetes is a chronic condition managed through lifestyle, insulin, and prescription medication.
While some herbs like bitter gourd or fenugreek may modestly assist glucose metabolism, no herbal medicine reverses or permanently cures diabetes.
Discontinuing medical therapy for diabetes in favor of unproven alternative or herbal remedies can lead to diabetic ketoacidosis and organ failure.
Handwashing with soap and clean water removes pathogens from hands and reduces the transmission of respiratory and diarrheal infections.
Effective hand hygiene practices in healthcare and community environments can reduce the spread of infectious diseases by up to 50%.
Drinking, gargling, or rinsing with salt water or vinegar does not kill the coronavirus and does not prevent COVID-19 infection.
Inhaling steam or taking extremely hot baths does not prevent or cure coronavirus infection and can cause severe thermal burns to airways.
Regular physical exercise, maintaining a healthy weight, and eating a balanced diet significantly reduce cardiovascular disease risk.
Garlic supplements and herbal teas cannot substitute for prescribed antihypertensive medication for controlling severe hypertension.
Fever is an immune response to fight infection; mild viral fevers resolve with hydration and rest, and antibiotics provide no benefit for viral fevers.
No alternative therapies, herbal concoctions, or alkaline diets have been proven to cure or eradicate malignant cancer tumors.
Pregnant women should always consult a licensed doctor before taking any herbal remedies, as many can induce premature contractions or toxicity.
Authorized COVID-19 vaccines have been shown to be safe and highly effective in preventing hospitalization and severe disease outcomes.
Depression is a legitimate medical disorder treated effectively with psychotherapy and prescription medication, not a lack of mental resolve.
No single food, vitamin megadose, or herbal supplement can instantly 'boost' the immune system to make a person immune to viral infections.
